questions.stem: Each try succeeds with chance 1/4. X = tries until the first success. E[X] is…
questions.incorrectFeedback: E[X] = 1/p = 4 (counting trials). Counting failures before the success gives q/p = 3, so check the support.

questions.stem: No six in the first 10 rolls of a fair die. The chance of a six on roll 11 is…
questions.correctFeedback: Yes — each roll is independent; the geometric wait is memoryless.
questions.incorrectFeedback: The die has no memory: given 10 misses, the next roll is still a six with chance 1/6. 'Due' is the gambler's fallacy.

questions.stem: Y = failures before the first success, with p = 1/5. E[Y] is…
questions.correctFeedback: Correct — failures convention: q/p = (4/5)/(1/5) = 4, one less than the 5 trials.
questions.incorrectFeedback: Failures before the first success: E[Y] = q/p = 4. The trials count X = Y + 1 has mean 5.

questions.stem: A fair coin. The chance the 2nd head comes on the 3rd toss is…
questions.correctFeedback: Right — toss 3 is a head and the first 2 hold exactly one head: C(2, 1)(1/2)³ = 2/8 = 1/4.
questions.incorrectFeedback: The last toss must be the 2nd head, and the first two tosses hold exactly one head (2 patterns): 2 × (1/2)³ = 1/4.

questions.stem: From Lesson 9: typos occur at 1 per 4 pages. What is λ for a 12-page document?
questions.incorrectFeedback: λ is the rate times the window's length: 1/4 per page × 12 pages = 3.
